To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the WA85 Experiment has shown that the production of Λ and Λ̅ particles in S-W collisions at 200 GeV/ c per nucleon follows a linear increase with the rapidity density in a region where the number of independent nucleon-nucleon collisions is expected to be between 70 and 140.

the production of Λ and Λ in the interaction of sulphur with tungsten nuclei at the CERN SPS at 200 GeV/ c is described in terms of a superposition of incoherent nucleon-nucleon interactions, that is to say, the production rate of these particles increases linearly with rapidity density, and that the ratio of Λ to Λ is approximately constant at 1.5.
the Λ and Λ production cross sections in 32S+W collisions at 200 AGeV/ c are (1.2±0.2) and (0.6±0.2)b, respectively.

the study of the properties of the nucleon in a nuclear environment and the study of dense hadronic matter.
understanding the structure and dynamics of the strong interactions.

the WA85 experiment has confirmed the predictions of the model based on the superposition of independent nucleon-nucleon interactions.

the production of $\bar{\Lambda} + \Lambda$ is not a linearly increasing function of the rapidity density, and that it does not follow a simple superposition model of independent NN collisions.
